A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same DMAP research work. Their complete main texts, Appendices A–O, equations, table, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original decoding-validation experiments, detector AUROC evaluations in Table 1, Pythia fine-tuning results, and appendix sensitivity and paraphrasing experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1, the fine-tuning experiments, and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: DMAP's interval construction, uniform sampling, and entropy-weighted variant are unchanged. Section 3.2 removes one occurrence of the recommended clipping value but retains the recommendation of lambda = 2 later in the section.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same datasets, domains, and tasks, including XSum, SQuAD, WritingPrompts, RAID, Ghostbusters, and OASST2. Prompt sensitivity and paraphrasing scenarios are unchanged; the Pythia model-size correction concerns settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT, and Binoculars in the same comparisons. Figure 12 also retains the comparison with probability integral transformation using random token ordering.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix K change the reported fine-tuning configurations from three Pythia sizes (70M, 410M, 1B) to two (410M, 1B). Figure 17's caption changes 1B to 410M, matching its existing identification in Appendix K.1. These are reported-setting corrections; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The convergence, entropy-group, prompt/cutoff sensitivity, random-order PIT, and DIPPER paraphrasing analyses retain the same experimental designs and plotted evidence. No supplementary test is added or removed.

E5.justification: The chi-squared testing procedure, p-value reporting, and finite-sample cautions are retained. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or other uncertainty reporting; Appendix D's statistic-to-distribution wording correction does not change the procedure.

E6.justification: All 54 AUROC values in Table 1 and the plotted distributions are retained. However, Figure 10's caption removes the qualitative finding that an initial cutoff of zero produces tail-heavy DMAP plots, retaining only the increased-variability finding.

T1.justification: Appendix B changes the nucleus-sampling definition from cumulative probability strictly greater than pi to greater than or equal to pi, changing the equality boundary. Proposition 3.1, its proof, and Proposition D.1 otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The conclusion explicitly restricts detector vulnerability to base models with pure sampling in the black-box setting. The introduction also specifies that unavailable internal probabilities belong to the generating model. The overall DMAP contribution and three applications remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B qualifies the near-flat top-k histogram shape as typical rather than unconditional. Section 5.3 revises the bias-propagation explanation and removes the explicit qualification distinguishing head bias in correct human responses from model overconfidence.

D1.justification: Appendix D drops the Python-specific description of statistical packages, and Appendix K/Figure 17 correct the model documentation. Preprocessing, prompt formatting, the lambda = 2 recommendation, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to PIT, text visualization, detection, and calibration research are unchanged. Reference-title capitalization and citation formatting edits do not introduce or remove related work.

P1.justification: V2 makes scattered grammatical, terminology, notation, and reference-formatting edits, rewrites a paragraph in Section 5.3, and changes Yoann L. Launay to Yoann Launay. Section organization and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The same 23 figures and Table 1 are retained, with several caption corrections, minor reflow, and an ICLR 2026 publication header. Figures 8 and 9 use lower-resolution embedded images but preserve their plotted content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reporting accuracy by reconciling the Pythia model count and Figure 17 attribution with the presented results, and better confines the detector-vulnerability conclusion to tested conditions. These gains outweigh the limited loss of the human-response overconfidence caveat. The methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is modest.
